verses.text: Joshua called together the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh.
He told them, “You've done everything Moses, the LORD's servant, commanded you, and you've listened to me in everything I told you to do.
All this time you've stayed with your fellow Israelites and carried out the duty the LORD your God gave you.
Now the LORD your God has given your fellow Israelites rest, just as he promised. So go back to your tents and to the land Moses, the LORD's servant, gave you across the Jordan.

Be very careful to follow the command and the law Moses, the LORD's servant, gave you. Love the LORD your God, follow all his ways, keep his commands, hold on to him, and serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Joshua blessed them and sent them home to their tents.

Moses had given half the tribe of Manasseh an inheritance in Bashan. Joshua gave the other half land among their fellow Israelites west of the Jordan. As he sent the eastern tribes back to their tents, he blessed them.
He told them, “Go home with all this wealth: plenty of livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and plenty of clothing. Share what you took from your enemies with your brothers.”
Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh left the other Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan and went back toward Gilead, the land they'd received as their own under the LORD's command through Moses.
When they reached the region near the Jordan in Canaan, Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh built an altar there by the river. It was big enough to make people stop and look.
The Israelites heard the news: “Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh have built an altar on the border of Canaan near the Jordan, on the side that belongs to Israel.”
When they heard, the whole Israelite community gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh in Gilead.
Ten leaders went with him, one from each tribe of Israel. Each was the head of his family among the clans of Israel.
They arrived in Gilead and spoke to the people of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
“The whole community of the LORD asks, ‘Why have you broken faith with the God of Israel? Why have you turned away from following the LORD today by building your own altar and rebelling against him?
Wasn't the sin at Peor enough for us? We still haven't cleansed ourselves from it, even after a plague struck the LORD's community.
Are you really going to turn away from following the LORD today? If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he'll be angry with the whole community of Israel.

If the land you received is unclean, cross into the LORD's own land, where his tabernacle stands, and take land among us. Don't rebel against the LORD or against us by building an altar besides the altar of the LORD our God.
Didn't Achan, a descendant of Zerah, break faith by taking what had been set apart? Anger fell on the whole community of Israel. Achan wasn't the only one who died because of his sin.’”
The people of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh answered the leaders of Israel's clans.
“The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD! He knows, and Israel will know. If we rebelled or broke faith with the LORD, don't save us today.
If we built this altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings, grain offerings, or peace offerings on it, may the LORD himself hold us accountable.
We did this because we were worried that one day your children might ask ours, ‘What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
The LORD made the Jordan a border between us and you people of Reuben and Gad. You have no share in the LORD.’ Then your children might make our children stop honoring the LORD.
So we said, ‘Let's build an altar, for a purpose other than burnt offerings or sacrifices.

It will serve as a witness between us and you, and between our descendants. It will show that we have a right to worship the LORD in his presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings.’ That way your children can't tell ours one day, ‘You have no share in the LORD.’

We thought, ‘If they ever say that to us or our descendants, we can answer, “Look at this copy of the LORD's altar that our ancestors made. It was built as a witness between us and you, with no burnt offerings or sacrifices made on it.”’

We would never rebel against the LORD or turn away from following him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices besides the altar of the LORD our God in front of his tabernacle!”
When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of Israel's clans with him heard what the people of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh said, they were satisfied.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest told the people of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, “Today we know the LORD is among us, because you haven't broken faith with him in this. You've saved the Israelites from the LORD's hand.”
Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left Reuben and Gad in Gilead, went back to the Israelites in Canaan, and told them what had happened.
The Israelites were glad and blessed God. They stopped talking about going to war against Reuben and Gad or destroying the land where they lived.
The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Witness Between Us That the LORD Is God.”
